bug_semantics: Unauthenticated stored XSS in the conversion graph: stored, attacker-controlled MISP/STIX fields became node labels, sublabels, edge labels, node types, node-property names and values, and edge-property values. CTI-Transmute passed those values as strings to Pivotick paths that resolved strings with HTML parsing, so viewing, hovering, or selecting a malicious graph item could execute markup/event handlers. Independently, Open raw JSON interpolated JSON.stringify(raw) inside a <pre> in win.document.write(), allowing crafted JSON text to terminate the element and inject executable markup into the new window.
flaw_origin: Commit 01837b8759efb57d85af9fc77341b406019643c5 first added the Pivotick conversion-graph feature and both unsafe data flows in website/web/templates/convert/detail.html: attacker-controlled graph fields were created around lines 722-800, returned as bare strings by nodeProperties beginning at line 831, passed to new window.Pivotick and its property maps around lines 978-1010, and raw JSON was interpolated into win.document.write at line 1046. Its direct parent 9b91aa6f52cd7da7ff66c5801e2a9fc7c37b66fe had no graph section or these sinks. Commit 11b0bc4583022cd863244af07040fcf5d9405738 later extracted substantially the same code into convertGraph.js and is therefore a move/refactor, not the BIC.
ai_marker: absent — the exact BIC commit object names author ecrou-exact <geffetheo@gmail.com> and committer ecrou-exact <geffetheo@gmail.com>; after the subject it contains no trailers, no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with marker, no bot identity, and no other AI attribution.
evidence: First-party advisory: https://api.github.com/advisories/GHSA-P8V9-H3M5-MVJ9 and https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p8v9-h3m5-mvj9 describe the Pivotick HTML-resolving paths, the document.write raw-JSON sink, the incomplete first remediation, and both fix commits. Source origin: git log -S'Open raw JSON' and git log -S'new window.Pivotick' identify 01837b8759efb57d85af9fc77341b406019643c5 as the first addition, followed by the later extraction 11b0bc4583022cd863244af07040fcf5d9405738; https://github.com/MISP/cti-transmute/commit/01837b8759efb57d85af9fc77341b406019643c5 adds website/web/templates/convert/detail.html lines 722-1046 containing the vulnerable field construction, bare-string Pivotick maps, and document.write interpolation. Direct-parent proof: the BIC commit object gives sole parent 9b91aa6f52cd7da7ff66c5801e2a9fc7c37b66fe, and git show/diff 9b91aa6f52cd7da7ff66c5801e2a9fc7c37b66fe..01837b8759efb57d85af9fc77341b406019643c5 shows the graph section and vulnerable lines entirely as additions to the existing template; the parent is also the v1.1 tag tip and contains no Pivotick graph construction, nodeProperties map, Open raw JSON action, or document.write sink. Fix evidence: https://github.com/MISP/cti-transmute/commit/b50451a746c9959efa508aeaa4a822d122687e35 first adds escapeGraphLabels before Pivotick and replaces the interpolated popup with DOM construction/textContent in website/web/static/js/graph/conversionGraph.js and graphSafety.js; https://github.com/MISP/cti-transmute/commit/d34ccac5d82a642389390187fb3455112cbce886 completes remediation by wrapping node/edge property cells with textContent-backed elements and sanitising node types. Version boundaries: git tag --contains 01837b8759efb57d85af9fc77341b406019643c5 returns v1.2, v1.3, v1.4, and v1.5, while both fix commits are contained only by v1.5; v1.1 resolves to the BIC parent. The first-party v1.2 release (https://github.com/MISP/cti-transmute/releases/tag/v1.2) announces the new graph, and the v1.5 release (https://github.com/MISP/cti-transmute/releases/tag/v1.5) explicitly lists CVE-2026-72751 as affecting 1.2-1.4 and says all security findings are remediated in v1.5. AI check: numactl-prefixed git cat-file commit 01837b8759efb57d85af9fc77341b406019643c5 shows only the human author/committer identities and subject, with no trailers or AI marker.
reasoning: The vulnerability begins with the first graph implementation, not with the later file extraction or subsequent rewrites. The BIC introduced the complete attack path in one normal, single-parent commit: stored conversion JSON supplied untrusted MISP/STIX display and property values; Pivotick received them as strings in HTML-parsing rendering paths, while the raw-object action directly embedded attacker data into an HTML string passed to document.write. The immediate parent is the v1.1 release tip and lacks the graph and every vulnerable sink, satisfying direct-parent absence. Later commit 11b0bc4583022cd863244af07040fcf5d9405738 merely moved the already-vulnerable graph code into a component. b50451a746c9959efa508aeaa4a822d122687e35 fixed labels and the raw popup but, as the advisory states, left property-panel and node-type paths; d34ccac5d82a642389390187fb3455112cbce886 closes those remaining paths and is therefore the complete direct fix. Tag ancestry and the repository's v1.5 release notes independently align the lifecycle: v1.1 is pre-BIC, v1.2-v1.4 are affected, and v1.5 contains both fixes. Finally, the only permissible AI-attribution source—the exact BIC commit object—has a non-bot author and committer and no AI/co-author/generated trailer, so the causal result is NOT_AI.
